confirmedRootCause.explanation: GFPGANer.enhance() (verified against the exact pinned gfpgan==1.3.8 tag source, gfpgan/utils.py) always returns a 3-tuple (cropped_faces, restored_faces, restored_img). Unpacking it into 2 variables raises 'ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2, got 3)' on every successful restore call, independent of GPU availability, weight validity, or environment configuration. This uncaught ValueError propagates to worker.py's generic 'except Exception: sys.exit(EXIT_INTERNAL)' handler (exit code 1), matching both observed canary failures exactly.
confirmedRootCause.reproductionMethod: empirical: monkeypatched worker.validate_weight/cuda_info/load_model to mock a CUDA-available environment and a stub GFPGANer whose enhance() returns a verified-shape 3-tuple, then called the real worker._run_restore() with the canonical fixture-equivalent tiny PNG. Reproduced 'ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2, got 3)' at worker.py:153 exactly. No GPU, torch, gfpgan, or RunPod call was required.
confirmedRootCause.secondaryConcernRuledOut: the canonical synthetic fixture has no real face, so facexlib's real-detection path (has_aligned=False) could plausibly detect zero faces; verified via source inspection that facexlib==0.3.0's paste_faces_to_input_image() handles a zero-face list gracefully (returns the background image, no exception) -- not a contributing cause
